newsitem.title: USA: Reynolds sees cost cuts/sales but Worsely expansion safe.
newsitem.headline: Reynolds sees cost cuts/sales but Worsely expansion safe.

text.p: Reynolds Metals Co expects its ongoing portfolio review to result in proceeds of about $900 million, chief executive Jeremiah Sheehan said on Wednesday.
He said the company was committed to a reduced capital spending program of $250 to $300 million per year, excluding acquisitions, over the next two years.

However, he said he does expect the reduced spending to include expansion of the 56 percent owned Worsley alumina plant in Western Australia to just under three million metric tonnes a year from 1.7 million.
"I could seek board approval (of Worsley) as soon as August," he said. The other 44 percent of Worsely is held by Gencor Ltd's Billiton division.
Sheehan told analysts Wednesday the company will use the proceeds to reduce debt, adding this will reduce annual interst expenses $70 to $75 million.
He said Reynolds had not yet reached a decision about our Can and Packaging businesses" and is considering various sale and spinoff options for all or a portion of these businesses.
"We expect to enter 1998 a dramatically improved company, repositioned for growth, against a backdrop of strong industry fundamentals," he said.
